_comment: Editor UI metadata for BOS. Overlaid onto the schema built from BosConfig (a SosFadeConfig superset). UI ONLY — never touches a trade decision or the source hash. Click Scan Strategies after editing. THE CONTRACT: `label` is the Pine input's TITLE and `desc` is its TOOLTIP, both verbatim from strategies/tradingview/bos_strategy.pine, changed in the same commit — one parameter, one name, one explanation, two UIs. They were EXTRACTED from the Pine by script rather than retyped, because a lab row saying something different from the chart is how a rule gets read backwards (exec_deep_fib said 'ABOVE' where its own tooltip said 'shallower', and that was false half the time). Params not listed here fall back to their raw field names; the inherited A+ fields that this fork pins are deliberately absent, because none of them is an input in this fork's Pine — see config.py for why each is pinned. COPY STYLE (2026-08-10, Aaron's call): every desc is SHORT and PLAIN — what the setting does, what each choice means, and the one fact that changes the decision. No measurement dumps, no trade counts, no R figures, no dates, no file references: the strategy detail page is for reading, and the evidence behind a default lives in this package's CLAUDE.md and its optimization doc. Same rule for `edge` and `steps`.
edge: A break of structure says the trend has turned. What comes after it is what this trades: the market keeps breaking in the same direction until it turns again, and each break gives a pullback to buy or sell into. The main bot fades the turn; this one rides what the turn started. Not every break is real, so it is filtered hard. Nothing here has been checked against the TradingView chart yet, so read the direction of a result and never the exact numbers.

steps.label: 01 · Turn
steps.title: A shift opens a run
steps.detail: Structure breaks and opens a run on that side. Until it does, nothing can trade.

steps.label: 02 · Break
steps.title: A continuation break sets up a trade
steps.detail: Each later break in the same direction is a fresh setup. The newest one always owns it — an older setup still waiting for its pullback is dropped.

steps.label: 03 · Pullback
steps.title: A limit rests in the pullback
steps.detail: An order rests at the chosen depth and fills the moment price touches it. The setup dies if price runs out of room or the time limit passes first.

steps.label: 04 · Manage
steps.title: Out at the last target or the stop
steps.detail: The first target moves the stop to breakeven and the second lifts it further. By default nothing is banked early: the whole position leaves at the last target, or at the stop that has been climbing behind it.

params.name: exec_longs
params.label: Trade longs
params.desc: Take long trades. Off = the long side never arms, and every long setup that was ready is logged as blocked, so you can still count what it cost.
params._desc_note: No tooltip on the Pine input — written here. Copy it back to the Pine before treating it as the shared text.

params.name: exec_shorts
params.label: Trade shorts
params.desc: Take short trades. Off = the short side never arms, and every short setup that was ready is logged as blocked.
params._desc_note: No tooltip on the Pine input — written here. Copy it back to the Pine before treating it as the shared text.

params.name: bos_which
params.label: Which break after the shift
params.desc: Which break after the turn to trade. The first is the initial push, the rest are continuations. A new break cancels an older setup still waiting.

params.name: bos_min_disp_atr
params.label: Break must clear the swing by (x ATR)
params.desc: How far the breaking candle must close past the level, in ATR. A one-tick poke is a stop run, not a break. 0 = accept any break.

params.name: bos_min_leg_atr
params.label: Break leg must be at least (x ATR)
params.desc: The smallest move that counts as a break, in ATR. 0 = no minimum.

params.name: bos_max_days
params.label: Drop an armed break after (days)
params.desc: How long a setup waits for its pullback before it is dropped. Counted in bars, so weekends and the daily close do not use it up.

params.name: bos_max_per_regime
params.label: Max trades between shifts
params.desc: Stop taking new trades after this many fills since the last turn. Lower it to stop losses stacking up in one choppy stretch.

params.name: bos_req_hold
params.label: Broken level must hold
params.desc: On = a close back through the broken level kills the setup. With an entry this deep that usually kills it just before it would have filled.

params.name: bos_fib_anchor
params.label: Measure levels on
params.desc: Which move the entry, stop and targets are measured on. Break leg freezes them at the break; expansion leg keeps moving until the pullback starts.

params.name: bos_entry_top
params.label: Shallowest the entry may rest
params.desc: The shallowest pullback the strategy will accept. Shallow entries fill far more often and pay far less.

params.name: bos_use_fvg
params.label: Price the entry off a gap
params.desc: On = the order is placed on a gap inside the pullback. Off = a plain level, and the settings below grey out.

params.name: exec_req_fvg
params.label: ↳ ...and require one (no gap = no trade)
params.desc: On = no qualifying gap means no trade. Off = it still trades, at the plain level below.

params.name: exec_fvg_deep_only
params.label: ↳ ...gap must sit fully past the shallow end
params.desc: On = the whole gap has to sit on the deep side of the shallow end. Better prices, reached less often.

params.name: exec_deep_fib
params.label: ↳ ...deep gap enters at the nearest fib
params.desc: For a gap deeper than 0.618, rest the order at the nearest level above it - the price you reach first.

params.name: exec_conf_sz2
params.label: ↳ ...Sniper Zone counts as a gap
params.desc: Lets the shallow pocket of the break stand in for a gap on a setup that had none.

params.name: exec_fvg_50
params.label: ↳ ...gap across the shallow end enters at it
params.desc: Last resort: a gap lying across the shallow end rests the order exactly on that line.

params.name: bos_entry_fib
params.label: Fallback entry level
params.desc: How deep in the pullback the order rests. This is what actually trades while gap pricing is off.

params.name: bos_respect_veto
params.label: Divergence blocks a new entry
params.desc: On = a long will not open while a bearish divergence is live or momentum is very overbought, and the mirror for shorts.

params.name: bos_vwap_req
params.label: Session VWAP filter
params.desc: Only trade while price is closing on the trend's own side of the session average price.

params.name: exec_no_late_day
params.label: No entries in the final hour (16:00-18:00 NY)
params.desc: Blocks new entries in the last hour before the daily close, so a trade cannot be gapped out over the break.

params.name: exec_htf_weekly
params.label: Weekly bias requirement
params.desc: Whether the weekly trend has to agree with the trade. Ignore = no filter.

params.name: exec_htf_daily
params.label: Daily bias requirement
params.desc: The same four choices, judged on the daily trend. Ignore = off.

params.name: exec_risk_pct
params.label: Risk % per trade
params.desc: How much of the account each trade risks. A wider stop automatically buys a smaller position.

params.name: bos_sl_model
params.label: Stop model
params.desc: Where the stop sits. ATR is a fixed distance from the entry and is the default.

params.name: bos_sl_atr
params.label: ↳ ATR multiple
params.desc: How far the stop sits from the entry, in ATR. Anything from about 1.2 to 1.5 gives the same answer.

params.name: exec_sl_buf_tk
params.label: Extra room beyond the stop (ticks)
params.desc: Pushes the stop this many ticks further away, so a wick through it does not take you out.

params.name: exec_min_stop_mode
params.label: Minimum stop distance
params.desc: Refuse a setup whose stop lands too close to the entry, which would buy an oversized position that noise runs straight through.

params.name: exec_min_stop_val
params.label: ↳ Minimum stop floor (unit = mode above)
params.desc: The floor itself. A percent, dollars of price, or an ATR multiple, following the mode above.

params.name: bos_move_stop
params.label: Moving stop (trails from entry)
params.desc: A trailing stop that starts as soon as you are filled. It follows the best price seen and can only tighten.

params.name: bos_move_stop_val
params.label: ↳ trail distance (unit = mode above)
params.desc: How far the moving stop sits behind the best price seen. Dollars of price in dollar mode, ticks behind the last swing in structure mode.

params.name: exec_tp1_pct
params.label: TP1 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the first target banks. 0 = bank nothing. Touching it still moves the stop to breakeven.

params.name: exec_tp2_pct
params.label: TP2 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the second target banks. 0 = bank nothing. Touching it still lifts the stop and hands the rest onward.

params.name: exec_tp3_pct
params.label: TP3 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the last target banks. 100 = the whole position leaves there, so there is no runner.

params.name: bos_tp3_measured
params.label: TP3 = measured move
params.desc: Replaces the last target with the size of the break projected forward from the level it broke. Ignored if it would land behind the second target.

params.name: exec_be_buf_tk
params.label: Breakeven buffer (ticks)
params.desc: How far past the entry the breakeven stop sits, so a scratch still covers costs.

params.name: exec_runner_trail
params.label: Runner trail method
params.desc: How the runner is trailed once the second target is hit. Structure parks the stop at the last swing; fixed step uses a dollar grid.

params.name: exec_struct_trail_buf_tk
params.label: ↳ Structure trail buffer (ticks)
params.desc: Structure method only. The trailing stop sits this many ticks beyond the swing it is following.

params.name: exec_trail_step
params.label: Runner trail step ($ of price)
params.desc: The step size in dollars. On gold 1 pip is 10 cents, so 50 pips = 5.0.

params.name: exec_tp2_stop_mode
params.label: TP2 → stop floor
params.desc: Where the stop jumps to the moment the second target is hit. TP1 is tight and can scratch the trade; breakeven gives it the most room.

params.name: bos_close_opp_div
params.label: Close an open trade on opposing divergence
params.desc: On = close the trade when a divergence confirms against it, rather than waiting for the stop or a target.
